conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to help you settle into motherhood and to check on how you’re feeling emotionally. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually shortened to the EPDS. It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; your answers stay between us and will guide any extra support you might need. If at any point you’d like to pause or clarify anything, just let me know. Ready to start?

First, thinking about the past week, how much of the time have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? It’s been kind of hard to laugh. I’ll smile if someone shows me a cute baby video or if my partner makes a joke, but it feels forced—like I’m doing it because I should, not because it comes naturally. Maybe once or twice I’ve actually giggled at something my older nephew did, but that’s about it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, but not very often. I’ll catch myself smiling if the baby does something cute or if my husband tries to be silly, but the laughter feels kind of flat—like I’m going through the motions more than really feeling it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk around the lake, even just binge-watching a show—but this past week nothing sounds that appealing. I’ll think “I should want to do that,” but when the time comes I’m too tired or it just feels like another chore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times. Yesterday the baby was fussy for almost an hour and I kept thinking maybe I’d eaten something that bothered him through my milk, or that I wasn’t holding him “right.” My partner finally said, “He’s just having a moment,” but I still felt like I must’ve done something. It’s not every day, but when stuff goes wrong my brain jumps to “this is probably my fault.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most days. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly wonder if his breathing sounds weird, or I’ll lie down at night and my mind races about SIDS, even though the pediatrician said everything looks fine. There isn’t a real reason—it’s just this low-level buzz in my chest like something bad could happen any second.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times. Mostly at night when the house is quiet—I’ll be walking to the kitchen for water and suddenly feel like I can’t catch my breath, heart pounding, like I need to run but I don’t know where. It only lasts a minute, and I know nothing’s actually wrong, but in that moment it feels like my body’s sounding a false alarm.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes—some days it feels like the pile never shrinks. I’ll finally finish a feeding and remember the laundry’s still in the washer, or the dog needs walking, or I haven’t eaten an actual meal since yesterday. I cope okay most of the time, but a couple afternoons I’ve just sat on the couch with the baby on my chest feeling like I’m drowning in small stuff.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not every night, but several nights this week I’ve lain there staring at the ceiling even when the baby’s out cold. My mind keeps circling: “Am I doing this right? Is he gaining enough weight? Should I pump more?” It takes me maybe an hour to finally drift off, and then he stirs half an hour later. So I’m not sleeping great, but it’s more because my brain won’t settle than because I’m horribly unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

Off and on—maybe every other day. I’ll be folding onesies and suddenly feel this heavy, weepy feeling, like a cloud parked itself over me. It usually lifts if the baby smiles or my partner hugs me, but it keeps popping back up.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really. I got a little teary on Wednesday when my mom left after visiting—just felt suddenly alone—but it never turned into full crying. My eyes might water for a minute, but I blink it away and move on.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I get tired and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like myself again and be a good mom.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – EPDS-Relevant Summary  

Patient: 0–2 wk postpartum; no current self-harm ideation.  

Symptoms endorsed (frequency/intensity)  
• Anhedonia / diminished pleasure (Q1, Q2)  
• Excessive guilt / self-blame (Q3)  
• Generalized anxiety & nocturnal rumination (Q4)  
• Discrete panic attacks (Q5)  
• Feeling overwhelmed / unable to cope (Q6)  
• Mood-linked insomnia (Q7)  
• Intermittent sad / weepy mood without full crying spells (Q8, Q9)  

Pattern: Sub-threshold depressive features plus prominent anxiety symptoms; no suicidal ideation.  

Screening significance  
Meets clinical threshold for possible postpartum anxiety; several EPDS items suggest depressive symptom overlap. Risk factors: sleep disruption secondary to mood, persistent worry, self-blame, impaired enjoyment.  

Observation: Recommend further evaluation for postpartum depression and anxiety; safety plan not indicated at present.
